Why we exist

“We are able to fix many different breakages that most optical shops will deem unrepairable.”

Very few optical shops will even attempt to restore old frames. We have the specialty equipment, processes and techniques they don’t keep in house, from PulseArc TIG welding under a microscope to heat-inserted splints for plastic, horn and wood.

Restoration stories

Arrived in pieces. Left whole.

Real before-and-after pairs from our plastic mending work. Every mending job is unique: the technique depends on the material, where it broke and how.

Case no. 01

A wood frame, broken clean through

Wood, horn and other exotic materials are handled case by case. We work on horn and wood frames from makers like Cartier, Rigards, Oliver Peoples, Feb 31st, Gold & Wood and Rolf.

WoodFrame mendingSun lenses

Case no. 02

Snapped acetate, mended from the inside

Don’t reach for super glue. It makes a repair more visible and can add cost to remove. We aim for mends that are as invisible as possible; transparent frames will usually show the internal splint.

AcetateInternal splint

Case no. 03

Three breaks, one pair of sunglasses

A broken bridge, a separated temple and a lens on the table. Hinges, rivets, spring and heat-sunk: we repair just about every type there is.

Hinge repairRebuild

From the restoration archive

Vintage metal re-straightened and refinished. Plastic sanded, filled and hand-worked back to matte, satin or high luster.

Heirlooms

They belonged to someone you loved.

Frames often carry sentimental value, whether they belonged to a beloved family member or they’re your own pair from years ago. We work with vintage and sentimental eyeglasses regularly, and we can bring them back to life.

  • Every pair is assessed before any work starts
  • Match the original color, or choose something completely new
  • Gold and palladium plating for vintage metal
  • Custom engraving or engraving restoration on qualifying acetate
  • New lenses, including sun lenses, cut for vintage frames

Sunglass conversions

Wear the keepsake. Outside.

Put custom sun lenses in a vintage or sentimental frame and it goes from the drawer back into daily life. Non-prescription and single-vision lenses are made for mail-in clients.

Custom tint

Bold, solid color in the shade you pick.

Gradient

Mix and match colors for a unique fade.

Mirrored

Stand out, or stay mysterious.

Polarized

Cuts glare off water, snow and road.

Lens materialsCR-39, Trivex, polycarbonate, high index, and real glass for those who want it.
Also availableTransitions lenses that darken in sunlight.
Bifocals & progressivesMade in person by appointment at Resurrection Eyewear, or for wholesale clients. We don’t do eye exams.

The shop

Industrial skill. Optical expertise.

Northwest Frame Repair is a family owned and operated business in the Pacific Northwest, just north of Seattle. It brings together Ryan’s industrial background and Tiffany’s extensive optical expertise, and we take extreme pride in our work.

Tiffany Tolle-Liberty, LDO, ABOC: licensed optician, nearly two decades in the industry
Customers in every U.S. state and multiple countries
Serving optical professionals and the public since 2012

Ryan & Tiffany

Partnered with American Optical. We repair and restore all of AO’s vintage models, and we hold all of the remaining new/old-stock inventory for the Original Pilot and the General: every size, color, lens and temple type ever made.
